Title: Ex-commando loses battle with leukaemia
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Former commando Sergeant Mohd Azuan Asmuni, whose battle with leukaemia drew the personal attention of Armed Forces chief General Tan Sri Malek Razak Sulaiman, has died after a prolonged fight against the disease.
Azuan, a former member of the 11th Special Service Regiment (11 SSR), died on Monday after being diagnosed with Acute Myeloid Leukaemia in 2023.
In a Facebook post,
Malek expressed sadness over Azuan's passing,
recalling his visit to the former commando's home on Feb 8.
Despite undergoing various treatments, Malek said Azuan had shown remarkable fighting spirit and resilience throughout his illness.
[[nid:1509712]]
"As a soldier shaped within the larger Gerak Khas family, he faced every challenge with courage and determination until the end of his life.
"A commando may have completed his duty in this world, but his fighting spirit, courage and resilience will live on in the memories of those who knew him," he said.
Malek also conveyed his condolences to Azuan's family and former comrades on behalf of the Armed Forces.
Azuan was buried at Felda Semenchu, Kota Tinggi, Johor.
He joined 11 SSR in June 2004 and completed 21 years of service in June 2025. During his service, he took part in training and operational duties and was active in endurance sports, including triathlons.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: MEF: Faster aid needed before viable MSMEs are forced to close
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The government must move faster to support viable micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) facing mounting cost and cash-flow pressures, or risk seeing temporary business difficulties turn into permanent closures and job losses.
Malaysian Employers Federation (MEF) president Datuk Syed Hussain Syed Husman said many MSMEs were not seeking permanent subsidies or special treatment, but simply needed enough "breathing space" to navigate a challenging operating environment.
Syed Hussain said the consequences of a viable MSME shutting down extended beyond the business owner.
"When an MSME closes, we do not lose only one business. We potentially lose jobs, suppliers, customers, local economic activity and an important part of Malaysia's entrepreneurial ecosystem.
"It is therefore far more sensible and cost-effective to help viable businesses survive a temporary period of difficulty than to deal with the economic and employment consequences after they have closed," he said in a statement.
Syed Hussain acknowledged that the government had already rolled out substantial support through its agencies.
However, he said the key issue was no longer simply how much funding had been announced, but how quickly it could reach businesses that needed it.
"For a small business struggling with cash flow, assistance received three or six months too late may no longer be assistance.
"By then, the business may already have accumulated arrears, lost employees, lost customers or ceased operations," he said.
MEF urged the government to examine measures adopted by other Asean economies to strengthen the resilience of smaller businesses.
Syed Hussain said the government should also consider temporary and targeted tax relief for viable MSMEs to complement existing financing measures.
MEF proposed a coordinated MSME survival and resilience package that includes temporary tax relief, faster access to financing, greater use of cash-flow-based lending and expanded government-backed guarantees.
The federation also called for temporary regulatory and compliance relief, faster payments to MSME suppliers by government agencies and government-linked companies (GLCs), greater access to government procurement and targeted support to help affected businesses retain employees.
"The success of an MSME support programme should ultimately be measured by businesses that remain open, workers who remain employed and entrepreneurs who become stronger and more competitive, not simply by the size of the allocation announced," Syed Hussain said.
MEF reiterated its readiness to work with relevant government agencies to ensure that MSME assistance is practical, accessible and responsive to actual business conditions.

Title: National Day, Malaysia Day corporate sponsorship surges to RM48.63mil, up 118pct
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: Corporate and private sector support for this year's National Day and Malaysia Day (HKHM) celebrations has more than doubled to RM48.63 million, up 118 per cent from RM22.3 million last year.
Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said the increase reflected growing private sector commitment to the celebrations.
He said 139 strategic partners from more than 350 organisations engaged by the ministry had contributed through cash, goods and services.
Of the total, RM2.7 million comprised cash contributions, which would be channelled into the Merdeka Secretariat Trust Account for the preparation and execution of the celebrations.
The remaining RM45.93 million comprised in-kind contributions in the form of goods and services.
"Based on the total sponsorship value, 50 per cent takes the form of promotional activities, 30 per cent comprises goods to be given to visitors, while the remaining 20 per cent represents sponsorship to the committees involved in organising HKHM 2026," he said at a sponsorship handover ceremony at Menara Komunikasi here today.
Fahmi said goods contributed by sponsors would be distributed by the ministry's volunteer team to attendees at the National Day celebration at Dataran Putrajaya on Aug 31 and Malaysia Day celebration at the Borneo Convention Centre Kuching in Sarawak on Sept 16.
He also announced that the Finance Ministry had approved the 2026 National Day and Malaysia Day celebrations as a national interest project under subsection 44(11C) of the Income Tax Act.
The approval allows individual and corporate sponsors to claim tax deductions of up to 10 per cent of their aggregate income for the current assessment year, subject to a RM15 million cap.
Given the significant increase in in-kind contributions this year, Fahmi said the Communications Ministry would appeal to the Finance Ministry to consider raising the tax incentive cap.
Meanwhile, all eligible Malaysian prepaid and postpaid subscribers of CelcomDigi, Maxis, TM, U Mobile and Yes will receive 10GB of free data under the Rahmah HKHM 2026 Rebate Incentive.
Fahmi said 5GB would be provided on National Day on Aug 31 and another 5GB on Malaysia Day on Sept 16.
Details on how to redeem the free data will be announced by the respective telecommunications companies, subject to their terms and conditions.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Tun M, Dr Siti Hasmah recognised as record-breaking centenarian couple
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Former prime minister Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamad and his wife, Tun Dr Siti Hasmah Mohd Ali, have made history after receiving three official records recognising their longevity and unprecedented achievements as a couple.
Dr Mahathir, 101, was recognised by Asean Records as the Oldest Living Former Prime Minister, while Dr Siti Hasmah, 100, was named the Oldest Living Spouse of a Former Prime Minister.
The couple were also jointly recognised by Asia Records as the First Former Head of Government and Spouse to Both Become Living Centenarians.
The records were presented at a ceremony held at the Perdana Leadership Foundation here yesterday by Advisory Board chairman Tan Sri Danny Ooi, accompanied by chief adjudicators Gillian Ooi and Eldrick Koh.
The conferment comes after a month of significant milestones for the couple, with Dr Mahathir celebrating his 101st birthday on July 10, followed by Dr Siti Hasmah's 100th birthday on July 12.
The couple also marked their 70th wedding anniversary on Aug 5.
The adjudication team also shared that verification found no equivalent achievement publicly documented across the Asean region and major Asian markets.
The three records recognise not only Dr Mahathir's longevity as a former national leader and Dr Siti Hasmah's milestone as his centenarian spouse, but also their shared distinction as a former head of government and spouse who have both reached 100 years of age while living.
The latest recognition adds another milestone to the couple's long public lives, which have spanned decades of Malaysia's modern history.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: All parties must learn from past management weaknesses in TH, says Zulkifli
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: All parties must learn from weaknesses and mistakes in the management of Lembaga Tabung Haji following the government's explanation in the Dewan Rakyat yesterday.
Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Religious Affairs) Dr Zulkifli Hasan said the government received various views, criticism, and condemnations from members of parliament during yesterday's special sitting.
However, he said the government's intention during the special sitting was to clarify the RCI report to Parliament and the public, highlighting various issues involving governance and integrity within TH.
"What the government is trying to do is explain, clarify, and shed light on the RCI report, nothing more than that
"This proves that we need to learn from weaknesses and mistakes. The RCI itself showed that among the causes of TH's failures and weaknesses were governance and integrity issues," he said.
He said this during his keynote address at the Multaqa Sidr Islamic Social Finance programme here today.
Yesterday, the Dewan Rakyat held a special sitting lasting more than 10 hours to discuss and debate the TH RCI Report concerning the institution's management and operations from 2014 to 2020, which was made public on July 29.
The session involved a briefing by Zulkifli, a debate by 39 MPs, and winding-up speeches by Zulkifli and Finance Minister II Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah Azizan.

Title: Couple charged in Ipoh court with trafficking MDMA
Article:
IPOH: A married couple was charged in the magistrate's court today with trafficking 480.6 grammes of Methylenedioxymethamphetamine last week.
Teoh Wai Loon, 44, and Lim Suk Pei, 38, nodded after the charge was read before magistrate S. Punitha.
No plea was recorded as drug trafficking cases fall under the jurisdiction of the High Court.
According to the charge, they were jointly accused of trafficking the drugs at a venue in Medan Bercham Bistari in the Kinta district at 10.30pm on Aug 4.
The charge was framed under Section 39B(1)(a) of the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952, read together with Section 34 of the Penal Code, which carries the death penalty or life imprisonment and whipping upon conviction.
The court fixed Dec 7 for case mention pending the chemical analysis report.
Deputy public prosecutor Muhammad Zulqarnain Wan Asmira appeared for the prosecution, while both accused were unrepresented.
On Aug 6, police arrested seven people, including the couple, for alleged involvement in a drug trafficking syndicate active since June following four raids in Ipoh and Tapah.
During the raids, police seized ketamine and MDMA, including 2.6kg of MDMA found at two houses in Tapah.
The total drug seizure was estimated at RM538,451, alongside three vehicles worth RM224,000 and RM32,376 in cash.

Title: Police expedite aid for family of officer killed in Sabah electric shock accident
Article:
KOTA BARU: Police will expedite benefits and welfare assistance for the family of Corporal Mohamad Nur Hafiz Rahim, 29, who died from electric shock last Thursday.
Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said the move aimed to ease the burden on the deceased's wife, who is raising their 2-year-old son.
He said today's visit to the family home was a gesture of sympathy from the entire police force.
Accompanying him were Bukit Aman Management director Datuk Seri Abdul Aziz Abdul Majid, Kelantan police chief Datuk Mohd Yusoff Mamat, and Sabah deputy police commissioner Datuk Mohd Azhar Hamin.
"We are here to convey the sympathies of the entire police force to the family of the deceased. The loss of any officer, regardless of rank or position, is a great loss to the police force," he told reporters after visiting the family at their home in Kampung Hutan Pasir, Ketereh.
Saifuddin Nasution said the assistance presented included contributions from the Sabah and Kelantan Police Contingents, as well as takaful payouts from the deceased's Police Cooperative contributions, totalling more than RM200,000.
He said the deceased had named his wife, Fatimah Shahira, as the beneficiary of his monthly pension, while his mother was also named a pension recipient.
He added that he instructed Bukit Aman to fast-track all other payments due to the family without subjecting them to standard administrative delays.
"I personally assured the wife and family that all matters relating to the process will be expedited and will not go through the standard procedure," he said, adding that the wife could contact the contingent headquarters for further welfare assistance.
Nur Hafiz and two other officers — Corporal Chiu Teck Siong, 40, and Constable Muhammad Raimi Ismarubee, 26 — died at 5.50pm last Thursday after suffering electric shocks while moving a metal pole outside the Weston Police Station near Sekolah Kebangsaan (SK) Weston in Beaufort, Sabah. — BERNAMA

Title: Perak DAP backs staying in unity government until end of term
Article:
IPOH: Perak DAP has unanimously decided to remain in the unity government and mobilise the party's entire machinery to fulfil the people's mandate and continue the country's reform agenda.
In a statement today, Perak DAP said the decision was made to deliver on its election promises under the leadership of Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.
According to the statement, Anwar's leadership had proven successful in implementing various reforms over the past three years, while also enhancing the country's image and standing on the world stage.
"DAP must continue to demonstrate its capabilities through achievements and work performance so as not to disappoint the people's expectations.
"By remaining in the government, we can continue implementing the Pakatan Harapan manifesto, including institutional reforms, judicial independence, efforts to combat corruption, reducing the cost of living, reforming the national revenue system, and safeguarding the rights and freedoms of Malaysia's multiracial society," the statement said.
Perak DAP stressed the need to fully realise the policies during the current term in order to drive reforms and spur national development for the people's well-being despite facing various challenges.
The party also remains committed to mobilising all its strength to fulfil the people's mandate while staying true to the aspirations of the "Malaysia for Malaysians" struggle and remaining mindful of its responsibility to that cause.
The statement also stressed that, to safeguard the political strength of an inclusive and progressive multiracial society, DAP needs to remain in the unity government to provide a balance and prevent extremist forces from continuing to gain ground.
"Malaysia has witnessed four changes of prime minister over the past seven years. Political instability has affected the economy and investor confidence. That bitter experience must not be repeated, and therefore DAP must not disappoint the mandate given by the people.
"The party must shoulder the responsibility of remaining in the Unity Government until the end of the term to maintain political stability, implement reforms, demonstrate achievements and regain the people's confidence. This is the right and responsible path," the statement said.
The position was expressed ahead of the 2026 DAP Party Conference this Sunday, which will determine whether the party remains in or leaves the federal government for the remainder of the current parliamentary term.
A motion on the matter will be tabled by DAP secretary-general Anthony Loke.
The motion will be decided through a vote involving 4,264 delegates from 1,704 eligible branches attending the conference at the Putrajaya International Convention Centre.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Four company directors claim trial over alleged fake Perkeso claims
Article:
MELAKA: Four company directors today claimed trial at the Ayer Keroh Sessions Court to charges of submitting documents containing false information to Social Security Organisation (Perkeso) officers to deceive the agency in 2024.
Alpha Buildcon director Henry Ratnaike, 45, faces four charges, while PK Tan Auto and Car Repair director Koh Kai Loon, 40, faces one charge.
Prima Kerjaya Trading director Gan Pay Kiat, 32, faces two charges, while fellow Alpha Buildcon director Ling Yate May, 58, faces four charges of abetting Henry.
The charges involve Daya Kerjaya 2.0 Employee Verification Forms containing allegedly false information, submitted with incentive claims under the Perkeso Daya Kerjaya 2.0 programme.
Henry allegedly committed the offences at Taman Merdeka Jaya, Batu Berendam, on May 10, 2024, while Koh allegedly committed his offence at Taman Kasawari Utama, Durian Tunggal, on June 14, 2024.
Gan allegedly committed the offences at Kompleks Perniagaan Kota Syahbandar on May 27 and 31, 2024, while Ling allegedly abetted Henry in the offences at Taman Merdeka Jaya on May 10, 2024.
Henry, Koh and Gan were charged under Section 18 of the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission Act 2009, while Ling was charged under Section 28(1)(c), read with Section 18 of the same Act.
If convicted, they face up to 20 years in jail and a fine of at least five times the value of the false particulars, or RM10,000, whichever is higher.
MACC deputy public prosecutor Sharina Farhana Nor Sa'ari proposed RM15,000 bail each, with the accused required to surrender their passports and report to the nearest MACC office monthly.
Judge Rohatul Akmar Abdullah granted bail of RM15,000 to Henry and Ling, RM9,000 to Koh and RM13,000 to Gan, with the additional conditions.
The court fixed Sept 14 for mention.
Henry was represented by lawyer FB Ng, while the other three were unrepresented.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Six express bus passengers injured in collision with trailer
Article:
BANDAR BAHARU: Six passengers were injured when an express bus collided with a trailer at Km169.2 of the North-South Expressway early today.
Bandar Baharu district police chief Superintendent Mohamad Sani Mat Ali said police received a call from the control room at 1.09am regarding the accident involving the two vehicles.
He said preliminary investigations revealed that the express bus, carrying nine passengers, was travelling from Alor Star to Kuala Lumpur.
"The express bus is believed to have crashed into the rear of a trailer laden with iron pipes travelling from Butterworth, Penang, to Shah Alam, Selangor.
"The bus driver is believed to have lost control of the vehicle before hitting the rear of the trailer.
"As a result, the second bus driver suffered injuries to his nose and is receiving treatment at Seberang Jaya Hospital in Penang, while the main driver was unhurt.
"Six passengers suffered minor injuries and received treatment at Sungai Bakap Hospital in Penang, while three other passengers escaped unhurt," he said when contacted today.
Sani said preliminary urine screening tests conducted on both the trailer driver and the express bus driver were negative for drugs.
He said investigations into the accident are being conducted under Section 43(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987.
"Those with information can contact the Bandar Baharu District Police Headquarters Traffic Enforcement and Investigation Division or contact traffic investigating officer Inspector Mohamad Aizzat Omar at 012-2461813.

Title: Jadi's RM35mil warrant proceeds hang in balance as shares lag exercise price
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Jadi Imaging Holdings Bhd looks unlikely to realise nearly RM35 million in potential proceeds from 699.64 million warrants expiring next month, with its shares currently trading below the warrants' exercise price.
At the time of writing, the product distributor's shares were trading at 3.5 sen, 1.5 sen below the five-sen price warrant holders must pay to convert each warrant into one new Jadi share.
In a notice to warrant holders filed with Bursa Malaysia today, Jadi described the warrants as "out-of-the-money", based on the 3.5-sen share price as at Aug 6, the latest practicable date.
The company said 699.64 million warrants remained outstanding as at Aug 6 and will expire at 5pm on Sept 14. Any warrants that are not exercised by the deadline will lapse, become null and void and cease to be exercisable.
At the five-sen exercise price, full conversion of the outstanding warrants could bring Jadi about RM34.98 million in fresh proceeds.
The potential proceeds are sizeable relative to Jadi's current financial position. The group had cash and bank balances of RM737,000 as at March 31, 2026, down from RM8.08 million a year earlier.
The warrants were issued free to entitled shareholders in September 2023 on the basis of one warrant for every two existing Jadi shares. Each warrant carries the right to subscribe for one new Jadi share at the exercise price.
When seeking shareholders' approval for the exercise in 2022, Jadi said the free warrants were intended to potentially provide funds for working capital as and when they were exercised, without incurring interest costs associated with bank borrowings.
Jadi's shares have traded between 1.5 sen and 8.5 sen since September 2023. Year to date, the stock has traded between 2.5 sen and five sen.
At the current 3.5-sen price, the shares would need to rise about 43 per cent to reach the warrants' five-sen exercise price.
Jadi said the last day for trading in the warrants will be Aug 26, with trading to be suspended from Aug 27.
Warrant holders will have until 5pm on Sept 14 to exercise their rights, after which any unexercised warrants will lapse.
The warrants will be removed from Bursa Malaysia's official list on Sept 15.
Jadi is principally involved in product distribution through online and offline channels, serving wholesalers, resellers and retailers across Malaysia.
Its product portfolio includes printer supplies, consumer electronics, personal care products, medical supplies and other consumer goods. Jadi's shareholders approved its diversification into consumer electronics in September 2024, while the group disposed of its manufacturing subsidiary in March 2025.
Jadi narrowed its net loss to RM956,000 in the fourth quarter ended March 31, 2026 from RM10.31 million a year earlier, when it recorded a RM10.19 million loss from a discontinued operation.
Excluding the discontinued operation, however, its loss from continuing operations widened from RM121,000 a year earlier, mainly due to weaker sales and year-end adjustments, including inventory write-downs arising from weak market demand.
Revenue fell 47.3 per cent to RM533,000 from RM1.01 million, which the group attributed to weaker demand for its existing products amid global economic challenges and intensified competition.
For the full financial year, Jadi's net loss narrowed 41.8 per cent to RM14.19 million from RM24.39 million in 2025, which included RM21.08 million in losses from discontinued operations.
Full-year revenue nearly halved to RM3.05 million from RM6 million.
Jadi said it remains focused on expanding its product portfolio, diversifying its customer base and widening its distribution channels.
It is also seeking to improve operational efficiency, after-sales support and brand visibility while maintaining prudent cash flow and working capital management amid market uncertainties.
As at March 31, Jadi's total liabilities stood at RM1.62 million, up 15.7 per cent from RM1.40 million a year earlier.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Two men jailed 14 days, fined RM8,000 each over fake MCs
Article:
KUANTAN: Two men were sentenced to 14 days in jail and fined RM8,000 each after pleading guilty to forging 40 medical certificates, at the magistrate's court here today.
Mohd Shukrie Zainuddin, 28, and Muhammad Asyraf Zunaidy, 31, will face an additional eight months in jail if they fail to pay the fine.
Magistrate Ellyna Othman handed down the sentence after the duo admitted to forging medical certificates purportedly issued by a clinic, using a doctor's name and signature to deceive others.
The offences were committed at a factory along Jalan Bypass Gebeng between March 28 and July 13.
They were charged under Section 465 of the Penal Code, which carries up to two years' imprisonment, a fine, or both upon conviction.
Deputy public prosecutor B. Deevagaran Naidu prosecuted, while the accused were represented by a National Legal Aid Foundation lawyer.
The lawyer had sought a fine, saying the accused had repented, while Deevagaran called for a deterrent sentence.
Ellyna ordered both men to serve the 14-day jail term from the date of their arrest.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Japan brushes off Australian PM's melon drama
Article:
TOKYO: Tokyo on Wednesday played down comments by Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese about melons gifted to him by his Japanese counterpart that have triggered a row Down Under, stressing the leaders' good relationship.
"We are aware of the reporting in the media. We have been informed by the Australian side that Prime Minister Albanese did not make the comments in the way that has been reported," a Japanese government statement said.
"In any case, the dinner hosted by Prime Minister Albanese during the Prime Minister's visit to Australia this May was held in a very relaxed atmosphere, and we believe it helped build a personal trust relationship between the two leaders," the statement added.
Albanese had already apologised over comments made during an interview last month with the comedy podcast Bush Deep in which he named Kylie Minogue as someone he would "shag."
But separate comments in the interview about the "strange" present of Japanese melons by Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi in May – when asked about his "most crap" diplomatic gift – this week sparked further uproar.
When the host asked if she'd "smuggled" the expensive fruit through Australian customs, Albanese held his hands up adjacent to his chest and said he "got a couple of melons."
"She came in looking like Pamela Anderson," the often provocative podcast's host Nikki Osborne replied, referring to the US actor and "Baywatch" star.
[[nid:1509651]]
Australia's opposition leader has called for Albanese to apologise over the "insulting" comments.
Asked whether he would say sorry for his "disrespectful behaviour" in parliament on Tuesday, the Australian leader said: "I reject the assertion in the question."
The comments prompted some outrage on social media in Japan, where Takaichi became the country's first woman prime minister last year.
"I'm not a supporter of the Liberal Democratic Party or a defender of the current government, but this is really awful. It's disrespectful towards our prime minister," said one X user.
"Sure this guy's remarks are unbelievable. On top of that, it suggests how he thinks it's OK to treat Takaichi – or Japan for that matter – this crudely," said another.
Some were also offended by the perceived insult to Japanese fruit, with the variety of melon in question costing upwards of 30,000 yen (US$190).
"Don't you dare think the Australian fruits and ours are the same. Ignorance is pathetic," said one social media comment.
Albanese for his part qualified his comments, saying that the fruit "ended up being quite good."
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Anwar to meet Brunei Sultan next week for 27th Leaders' Consultation
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim will meet Brunei Sultan Hassanal Bolkiah in Bandar Seri Begawan next week for the 27th Annual Leaders' Consultation (ALC) between Malaysia and Brunei.
Anwar said he received a telephone call from the Sultan, who asked about his wellbeing and prayed for his health.
"I am grateful for His Majesty's prayers and concern," he said in a Facebook post today.
Anwar said he also prayed for the Sultan's continued good health and wellbeing.
"God willing, I will have an audience with His Majesty next week in Bandar Seri Begawan in conjunction with the 27th Annual Leaders' Consultation between Malaysia and Brunei Darussalam," he said.
The ALC is the highest bilateral mechanism between the two countries, providing a platform for the leaders to review cooperation and discuss regional and international issues of mutual interest.
The meeting comes
shortly
after Anwar underwent an elective laparoscopic procedure for an abdominal hernia on Aug 10.
His medical team head Datuk Dr Asri Rangga Abdullah Ramaiah said the procedure was completed smoothly under the care of medical specialists.
Anwar is expected to remain under medical observation for two days following the procedure.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Putin threatens retaliatory seizures of European ships
Article:
MOSCOW: Russian President Vladimir Putin on Wednesday threatened to seize ships belonging to European countries in retaliation for plans to sell off cargo seized from Russian "shadow fleet" vessels.
Several European companies have intercepted ships carrying Russian oil in contravention of European sanctions targeting the vital revenue source.
New sanctions passed last month permit EU members to sell the oil or any other cargo seized from the ships.
Moscow has bristled at the moves, with Putin calling it "piracy and banditry."
"We will be forced to respond in kind," the Kremlin chief said while overseeing naval drills in Russia's Far East.
Moscow would act "wherever we ourselves deem necessary and appropriate – anywhere," he added.
Swedish court documents obtained by AFP earlier in August showed Stockholm will transfer to Kyiv a seized Russian ship suspected of transporting grain from occupied Ukraine.
Putin was speaking aboard the Russian cruiser Varyag off the island of Sakhalin, where Russia's navy was conducting drills.
The exercises come a week before joint US-South Korean war games, designed to simulate a possible invasion from North Korea.
Tensions are high in the region amid accusations from Kyiv and Seoul that Pyongyang and Moscow are further intensifying their military cooperation.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: KLIA flights to be suspended during National Day flypast rehearsals
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: Take-offs and landings at Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) will be temporarily suspended during rehearsals and the National Day flypast as airspace within the Kuala Lumpur Terminal Control Area is closed on selected dates.
The Civil Aviation Authority of Malaysia (CAAM) said the airspace would be closed from Aug 26 to 29 and on Aug 31 to facilitate rehearsals and the National Day flypast in Putrajaya.
In a statement today, CAAM said the closures were necessary to ensure the safe and orderly conduct of the rehearsals and flypast.
The schedule is as follows:
Aug 26 to 28: Airspace closed from 11am to noon for rehearsals.
Aug 29: Full rehearsal from 8.45am to 9.45am.
Aug 31: National Day flypast from 8.45am to 9.45am.
Passengers travelling through KLIA during the affected periods are advised to check their flight status and schedules directly with their respective airlines, as some flights may be rescheduled or otherwise affected by the temporary suspension of aircraft movements.
CAAM also reminded the public that drone or unmanned aircraft system operations are strictly prohibited within the affected areas during the rehearsals and flypast.
"Unauthorised drone operations pose a serious safety risk, particularly to aircraft operating at lower altitudes and may result in enforcement action under the Civil Aviation Regulations 2016," it said.
CAAM said the temporary measures were necessary to safeguard the safety, security and efficiency of Malaysia's airspace during the National Day flypast.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Nanta to leave Parliament, eyes state assembly seat
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Works Minister Datuk Seri Alexander Nanta Linggi will not defend his Kapit parliamentary seat in the next general election (GE16).
Nanta, who is also Gabungan Parti Sarawak (GPS) secretary-general, however said he would remain in politics. He has served as Kapit member of parliament since 1999.
He plans to contest a new state assembly seat within the Kapit constituency if it is gazetted ahead of the next Sarawak election.
The Election Commission (EC) was previously reported to be finalising a proposal to redraw Sarawak's electoral boundaries, which includes 17 proposed new state seats.
"I have actually been quite firm about giving up this parliamentary seat. I am not retiring from politics, but may continue my political struggle through other means and no longer as an MP.
"I have been an MP for almost 30 years. I have held various positions, including deputy rural development minister, domestic trade and cost of living minister and now works minister.
"I feel it is time we gave the younger generation a chance in Parliament," Nanta said.
Nanta added that it was time for him to focus on state-level development, particularly in Kapit, even if he was no longer an MP.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: RM300mil paint shop puts Inokom in pole position for automotive growth
Article:
INOKOM Corp Sdn Bhd has strengthened its manufacturing capabilities with the launch of Paint Shop 3 (PS3), a RM300 million investment aimed at boosting production capacity, technology transfer and sustainable automotive manufacturing in Malaysia.
Launched by Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani on Tuesday, PS3 is one of Sime's largest manufacturing investments to date and is operated by a 100 per cent Malaysian workforce.
The facility can produce up to 50,000 painted vehicle bodies annually on a two-shift operation, lifting Inokom's combined paint-shop capacity to 100,000 units a year.
It is also equipped to paint plastic components and can support multiple vehicle models, giving the company greater flexibility to respond to market demand and future programmes.
"Inokom has evolved alongside the National Automotive Policy," said Inokom director Tan Sri Ben Yeoh.
"From our beginnings as part of the nation's automotive development ambitions, we have grown into a trusted manufacturing partner for global automotive brands.
"PS3 reflects our continued commitment to investing in local capabilities, technology transfer and the future growth of Malaysia's automotive industry," he added.
Automation is at the heart of PS3, with 32 painting and sealant robots, a fully automated pre-treatment and electrodeposition line, advanced spray booths and an integrated conveyor system.
Its Cartridge Bell System enables colour changes in under 10 seconds and supports up to 27 colour variants, improving efficiency and reducing downtime.
"PS3 is a significant enhancement to Inokom's manufacturing ecosystem. The facility expands our painting capacity, increases production flexibility and strengthens our ability to support the evolving requirements of our customers," said Syed Ahmad Muzri Syed Faiz, managing director of Sime Motors' assembly and strategic businesses.
Designed with sustainability in mind, PS3 features a Regenerative Thermal Oxidiser system that cuts CO₂ emissions by approximately 60 per cent, while its dry scrubber eliminates water use in spray-booth operations.
The facility is also ready for waterborne paint technology.
Inokom said its collaboration with Mazda's technical team has further enabled knowledge transfer, training and engineering expertise.
This strengthens Inokom's capabilities and supporting Malaysia's ambitions for a more advanced and sustainable automotive manufacturing ecosystem.

Title: Navigating choppy geopolitics requires a multi-faceted strategic balancing act
Article:
UNVEILING the 13th Malaysia Plan in parliament on July 31st, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim underlined the importance of regional security to Malaysia's 2026-2030 development roadmap.
He singled out the South China Sea, declaring that Malaysia's "readiness to confront sovereignty and security threats in the South China Sea will be intensified more comprehensively."
Without naming specific countries, the Prime Minister's statement reflects a clear understanding that the strategic environment in the Asia-Pacific is becoming increasingly dangerous.
China, which is Kuala Lumpur's largest trading partner and with which it shares deep historic and cultural connections, is becoming more assertive in the region, matched by record defence spending.
Of real concern for Putrajaya are Beijing's infringements on its maritime sovereignty. Last year, the China Coast Guard (CCG) spent 261 days in the northeastern area of Malaysia's Exclusive Economic Zone (EEZ).
While Putrajaya should maintain its close relationship with China, it is rightly preparing for an increasingly contested region.
Deeper defence relationships with like-minded nations – Australia and Japan stand out as logical partners - are the best way forward.
In a sign that Putrajaya is taking sound steps, Malaysian firm Westar Defence Industries formalised collaboration with Australian defence company Rocket Technologies last month, which will enable Malaysia to start manufacturing rockets domestically by 2028.
The agreement came during Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin's working visit to Australia in early July.
Commenting on the agreement, the defence minister captured its importance: "This initiative will not only strengthen industrial capability but also contribute to the development of a sustainable and competitive domestic defence sector."
Indeed, the development of Malaysia's domestic defence industry is crucial given that countries can withdraw from agreements at any time.
Norway's surprise decision to revoke export licences for the Naval Strike Missile system destined for Malaysia's littoral combat ship programme is a recent and sore example.
The Rocket Technologies-Westar Defence Industries agreement is exactly the kind of partnership Malaysia should seek to replicate.
Putrajaya and Canberra's collaboration is not limited to just equipment transfers. In early May, the two nations carried out the Malaysia-Australia Training Exercise (MASTEX) off Australia's west coast, a naval exercise that strengthened operational integration and cooperation.
Malaysia has also continued to deepen its defence cooperation and exchanges with Japan, another standout security partner. Officials from Malaysia's Ministry of Defence and armed forces observed the Michinoku Alert humanitarian assistance and disaster relief exercise held in Japan in 2024.
The MALPAN bilateral naval exercise conducted in April this year demonstrated that the two countries continue to strengthen their defence cooperation while steadily building operational trust.
[[nid:1509628]]
Malaysia should continue to deepen interoperability through more naval, land and air exercises with Japan and Australia. Combat-ready forces and relationships will be key to defending Putrajaya's sovereignty.
Elevated Japan-Malaysia defence cooperation has been underpinned by the Comprehensive Strategic Partnership, signed in 2023.
Indeed, as evidence of the strong partnership, in late 2025, Tokyo supplied Putrajaya with 14 unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) and seven rescue boats under its Official Security Assistance (OSA) programme.
Malaysia is also charting its own path towards improving its deterrence capability and security. Earlier this year, Prime Minister Anwar warned that, amid escalating global tensions, Malaysia cannot take its security for granted.
Putrajaya is pursuing asymmetrical warfare capabilities, focusing on low-cost, mass-produced weapons such as drones and rockets.
While Putrajaya-Tokyo defence cooperation is necessary, the partnership is broader than just security, ranging from industry to energy and more.
In March, the Embassy of Japan in Malaysia hosted an industrial cooperation seminar, bringing together senior government figures and industry leaders.
In May, Daihatsu announced that it would begin manufacturing hybrid vehicles (HV) at the plant of Malaysia's largest automaker, Perodua, marking its first overseas HV production.
The agreement was welcomed by Anwar and Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi in a joint statement following their June meeting in Tokyo. Energy cooperation is another important pillar of the Japan-Malaysia partnership.
Putrajaya has signed a letter of intent on cooperation in energy security under the Japan-led POWERR Asia initiative, which seeks to secure energy supply chains and counter disruptions.
The agreement is already yielding dividends, and Petronas announced in June that it will supply JERA, Japan's largest power generation company, with two million metric tonnes of liquefied natural gas per year for 20 years.
Putrajaya and Tokyo's growing practical cooperation across energy, industry and defence is a step in the right direction, and the partnership is guided by a mutual understanding of what the regional order should look like.
The Free and Open Indo-Pacific (FOIP) vision, originally developed by the late former Japanese Prime Minister Shinzo Abe, and Asean's Outlook on the Indo-Pacific (AOIP), which Malaysia is a key proponent of, both emphasise freedom of navigation and opposition to coercion.
Malaysia must continue pursuing deepened cooperation with partners that value its sovereignty. This will allow Putrajaya to navigate through choppy geopolitical waters, which the two superpowers have done little to calm.
* The writer is Principal Consultant at Arunachala Research & Consultancy Sdn Bhd (ARRESCON), a think tank specialising in strategic and geopolitical analysis

Title: Kedah Pas vows to continue fight against gambling despite court ruling
Article:
ALOR STAR: Kedah Pas has vowed to continue its fight to eliminate gambling in the state despite the Federal Court's dismissal of the state government's bid to appeal a ruling against its ban on issuing and renewing gambling premises licences.
Kedah Pas commissioner Datuk Ahmad Yahaya said the party accepted the court's decision, while expressing disappointment over the outcome.
He said the ruling meant the High Court's June 2024 decision, which struck down Kedah's zero-gambling policy, remained in force.
"Kedah Pas takes note of the Federal Court's decision to reject the Kedah government's application for leave to appeal over the cessation of gambling premises licences.
"We are saddened by the decision, although we respect the court's ruling," he said in a statement today.
The Federal Court today
dismissed
the Kedah government's application for leave to appeal a ruling declaring its directive not to issue or renew business licences for gambling activities unconstitutional.
A three-member bench led by Datuk Rhodzariah Bujang, with Datuk Collin Lawrence Sequerah and Datuk Azmi Ariffin, unanimously dismissed the application after finding that the questions of law raised did not meet the threshold under Section 96(a) of the Courts of Judicature Act 1964.
Ahmad, who is also Pokok Sena MP, said Kedah Pas considered the state government's efforts to prevent social ills through the policy justified.
However, he regretted that certain parties had challenged the move, resulting in the matter being brought to court.
"How can there still be parties determined to defend the crime of gambling in the state, despite the state government's efforts to shut down all premises being carried out within the existing legal framework?
"Kedah Pas reiterates that the principle of amar makruf nahi mungkar (enjoining good and forbidding evil) will continue to be upheld in governance," he said.
Ahmad said it also fully supported the state government in taking any appropriate follow-up action following the Federal Court's decision.
"God willing, the struggle will not end here," he said.
The Kedah government previously announced that it would stop issuing licences for gambling premises from Jan 1, 2023, following a decision by the state executive council on Dec 8, 2021.

Title: Teach children to speak up, disagree with respect, says Fadhlina
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Education should not merely teach children to be well-behaved, but also give them the confidence to speak up, think critically and disagree respectfully, says Education Minister Fadhlina Sidek.
She said character education should equip students to articulate their views, challenge opposing opinions and defend their positions without compromising courtesy.
"Character education is not just about teaching children to be good. We want them to be brave to speak up, think critically and remain respectful when they have differing views.
"This is the kind of character education we want to nurture," she said in a Facebook post after attending the national-level Madani Youth Forum today.
Fadhlina said the forum demonstrated how young people could build confidence in using Bahasa Melayu while developing their ability to argue and engage with differing views.
She said the students were articulate and composed, able to build arguments and challenge their opponents without losing their sense of courtesy.
"What happened on stage was much bigger than a competition. These children were learning how to think before they speak, organise their thoughts, state their positions, listen to different views and defend their arguments," she said.
Fadhlina said efforts to uphold Bahasa Melayu should focus on giving young people more opportunities to use the language, rather than merely asking them to love it.
She said a mature nation was not built by a generation that agreed on everything, but by one that knew how to disagree constructively.
"Our task is not to determine what they should say. Our task is to ensure that when it is their turn to speak, they have the knowledge to argue and the courtesy to listen," she said.

Title: Kelantan rewards Muay Thai fighter Aliff Rakib RM20,000 after ONE Championship triumph
Article:
KOTA BARU: Muay Thai fighter Ahmad Nor Iman Aliff Rakib today received RM20,000 from the Kelantan government in recognition of his historic ONE Championship victory last month.
The mock cheque was presented by Kelantan Menteri Besar Datuk Mohd Nassuruddin Daud at a ceremony held at JKR 10 here today.
The Rantau Panjang-born fighter, better known as Aliff Rakib, made history last month when he knocked out Thai legend Sam-A Gaiyanghadao in the fifth round at Lumpinee Stadium in Bangkok to win the ONE Interim Strawweight Muay Thai World Championship.
The victory made Aliff the first Malaysian fighter to win a Muay Thai world championship belt in ONE Championship.
Nassuruddin said the state government would continue to provide assistance within its means to recognise and support Kelantan athletes who bring pride to the state and country.
"We will give according to our ability and the resources available to us.
"Congratulations and thank you to Aliff for bringing pride to Kelantan," he said.
Aliff expressed his appreciation for the recognition, saying the sacrifices and financial burden borne by his family throughout his sporting journey were known only to him and his family.
"Thank you to the state government. Before this, only my family knew the sacrifices and burden we had to bear.
"After this, I hope the state government can continue to support me in whatever ways possible," he said.
Aliff said he remained determined to continue his efforts and hoped to achieve greater success for Malaysia on the international stage.
"InsyaAllah, Malaysia can," he said.
Following his historic victory, Aliff is now targeting a title unification bout against undisputed strawweight Muay Thai world champion Prajanchai PK Saenchai in October.
The 22-year-old will be aiming to build on his breakthrough victory and become the undisputed ONE Strawweight Muay Thai World Champion.

Title: Influencer avoids jail, bound over for promoting online gambling
Article:
MARANG: A female influencer escaped a jail term after the magistrate's court here today ordered her to be bound over for good behaviour for two years on a RM2,000 bond after she pleaded guilty to promoting online gambling.
Magistrate Nur Athirah Hashim imposed the order on Nur Syakilla Natasya Sukri, 20, after considering a Social Welfare Department report and submissions from the defence.
The court was informed by Assistant Social Welfare Officer Shahrizal Ali that a social report was prepared because the accused, aged under 21, is classified as a young offender, to assist the court in evaluating her background and personal circumstances before sentencing.
According to the report, investigations revealed that the accused suffered a thigh injury that rendered her unable to perform heavy work.
The report also noted that the accused was reclusive, had few friends, and rarely left home, with the department assuring that her family is capable of monitoring her conduct.
Nur Syakilla was charged with promoting online gambling featuring betting elements at 12.45pm on Jan 23, 2026, in the vicinity of Pasar Marang.
She was charged under Section 4(1)(g) of the Common Gaming Houses Act 1953, which carries a fine of between RM5,000 and RM50,000, or a prison sentence of up to three years, upon conviction.
The court took into account that it was her first offence before ordering the two-year good behaviour bond.
The court said the order was intended to give her a second chance while serving as a reminder to social media influencers not to be tempted by lucrative offers to promote online gambling.
Deputy public prosecutor Nur Sarah Syamimi Safie appeared for the prosecution, while the accused was represented by lawyer Muhamad Ramlan Taib.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Act now before haze turns into crisis – Lee Lam Thye
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia must act early to prevent worsening transboundary haze from developing into a national crisis, says Alliance for a Safe Community chairman Tan Sri Lee Lam Thye.
He said unhealthy air quality in parts of Sarawak and deteriorating conditions in parts of Peninsular Malaysia should serve as an early warning for the government to prepare for another serious haze episode.
"The present situation in Sarawak is particularly worrying because prolonged hot and dry weather creates conditions in which fires can spread rapidly and smoke can travel across borders," he said in a statement today.
Lee said above-normal temperatures and below-normal rainfall forecast across parts of Southeast Asia could further increase the risk of fires and haze.
He urged the government to adopt a preventive approach by strengthening hotspot and air-quality monitoring, and fully activating the National Haze Action Plan when risk indicators rise.
Malaysia should also intensify cooperation with Indonesia and other Asean countries under the Asean Agreement on Transboundary Haze Pollution, he said.
"What we need now is stronger implementation and faster action on the ground," he said.
Lee also called for greater attention to local sources of haze, including open burning, peat fires, agricultural burning and poorly managed land clearing.
"Haze should no longer be treated as an annual seasonal inconvenience. It should be treated as a recurring regional disaster risk that requires year-round prevention, preparedness and cooperation," he said.
He urged authorities to provide clear protocols and timely information for schools, hospitals, workplaces, vulnerable groups and outdoor workers when air quality deteriorates.
"Prevention is cheaper than dealing with the consequences. The time to prepare for the next haze crisis is before the skies turn grey, not after," he said.

Title: Kerjaya Prospek lands RM223mil Johor contract
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Kerjaya Prospek Group Bhd has secured a RM223 million contract from Sunway Majestic Sdn Bhd to construct a 1,012-unit Small Office/Home Office development in Johor Bahru.
The contract, awarded to its wholly-owned subsidiary Kerjaya Prospek (M) Sdn Bhd, covers the main building works for two 34-storey buildings, a 10-level podium car park and two levels of mezzanine commercial space.
Construction is scheduled to begin on Sept 1, 2026, and is expected to take 32 months.
Kerjaya said the latest win is its ninth contract in the financial year 2026 (FY26) and its third project in Johor Bahru since 2025, strengthening its presence in the southern region.
Kerjaya Prospek chief executive officer and executive director Tee Eng Tiong said the company's year-to-date FY26 contract wins have reached RM2.4 billion, exceeding its initial RM2 billion target for the year.
"Together with our total outstanding order book of RM5 billion, this provides us with strong earnings visibility over the coming years," he added.

Title: Kelantan sets up vehicle to tap oil and gas sector
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Kelantan state government has established a special purpose vehicle, Kelantan Ventures Sdn Bhd (KVSB), to strengthen the state's involvement in the oil and gas industry.
Deputy Menteri Besar Datuk Dr Mohamed Fadzli Hassan said KVSB aims to ensure that the people could benefit from the initiative while contributing to the state's sustainable economic development.
"However, the approach must consider the existing legal framework, including the Petroleum Development Act 1974, as well as the different constitutional position compared with Sarawak, which has certain rights under the Malaysia Agreement 1963 (MA63)," he said at the Dewan Undangan Negeri sitting in a response to a question from Mohamad Nasriff Daud @ Daud Yatimee.
Fadzli added that the state government is building capacity, exploring investment opportunities and establishing partnerships with reputable companies across the industry's value chain.
"The participation focuses on developing the oil and gas industry value chain, including the development of supply bases, logistics, upstream and downstream support services, as well as exploring opportunities in the energy sector.
"This approach is in line with developments in the Northern Offshore Oil & Gas Corridor, which places the Tok Bali Supply Base (TBSB) and Tok Bali Industrial Park (TBIP), together with future integration with the logistics network of the East Coast Rail Link (ECRL), at the centre of these efforts," he said.

Title: ACCCIM backs Building Managers Act as property management grows more complex
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Associated Chinese Chambers of Commerce and Industry of Malaysia (ACCCIM) has lauded the proposed Building Managers Act, describing it as a timely move to address the growing complexity of managing stratified and mixed-use developments across the country.
The association said such developments require increasingly specialised management due to multiple ownership structures, different property uses and more sophisticated building systems.
"This Act is overdue in light of the increasing development of stratified buildings and also the development of mixed-use integrated developments requiring more complex management of such buildings owned by multiple owners and integrated buildings of different usage.
"A well-managed and maintained building will preserve and enhance property values and investments for the benefit of property owners," it said in a statement.
ACCCIM said the rapid growth of stratified developments, coupled with the increasing adoption of technology, automation and energy-efficient systems, has created demand for building managers with specialised and multidisciplinary skills.
It said modern building management requires expertise across multiple disciplines, supported by continuous training and professional development to keep pace with evolving industry requirements.
Against this backdrop, ACCCIM said the proposed Act is a natural extension of the Housing and Local Government Ministry's oversight of areas such as building approvals, fire safety, health regulations and strata management.
The proposed board would be responsible for registering and categorising qualified building managers from academic and professional backgrounds, as well as experienced practitioners who have acquired their skills through industry experience.
"This will create a growing pool of talent and experienced practitioners to complement the growing need from the development of more and more stratified buildings," it said.
ACCCIM expects the proposed law to improve management and maintenance standards across residential and commercial properties, helping to preserve asset values and create more sustainable living and working environments.
The Housing and Local Government Ministry on Monday announced plans to introduce and amend four housing laws under the National Housing Policy 2026-2035 as part of efforts to establish a more comprehensive, forward-looking and equitable legal framework.
Minister Nga Kor Ming said the initiative involves three new laws — the Property Development Act, Building Managers Act and Rent Tenancy Act — as well as amendments to the existing Strata Management Act 2013.

Title: Haze hits Malaysia as 12 air monitoring stations record unhealthy API readings
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 12 — Malaysia has been experiencing haze since Aug 8, with 11 air monitoring stations recording unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings and one station in Sarawak recording a very unhealthy reading as of 3pm today, the Ministry of Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability (NRES) said.
In a statement today, the ministry said the El Niño phenomenon occurring alongside the Southwest Monsoon had resulted in several areas, particularly southern Peninsular Malaysia and western and southern Sarawak, receiving below-average rainfall.
The combination of lower rainfall and higher temperatures could increase the risk of water shortages, forest and peat fires, as well as haze, particularly in areas experiencing prolonged dry conditions, it said.
As of 3pm today, 11 of the 68 air quality monitoring stations recorded unhealthy API readings. These were Cheras in Kuala Lumpur (122), Putrajaya (121), Shah Alam in Selangor (112), and in Sarawak, Miri (152), Samalaju (120), Bintulu (154), Sibu (135), Sarikei (161), Sri Aman (158), Samarahan (177) and Kuching (177).
The Sarawak station at Serian recorded a very unhealthy API reading of 204.
NRES said the deterioration in air quality in Sarawak was caused by transboundary haze as well as local fires at a waste disposal site under the supervision of the Sibu Municipal Council, covering an estimated 1.5 hectares, and forest and bush fires in Sri Aman covering about 100 hectares. Firefighting operations were ongoing at both locations.
Based on the Regional Haze Map and information issued by the Asean Specialised Meteorological Centre (ASMC) today, dry conditions were observed across southern Asean, except in parts of northern Sumatra where rain was reported.
Isolated hotspots were detected in central and southern Sumatra, as well as southern and eastern Kalimantan, with several hotspots also detected in Peninsular Malaysia, Sarawak, Java and Sulawesi.
Moderate smoke plumes were observed in West Kalimantan and Central Kalimantan, while light smoke plumes were observed in southern Sumatra.
Based on NOAA-20 satellite monitoring on Aug 11, 12 hotspots were detected in Malaysia, comprising one in Pahang and 11 in Sarawak. A total of 60 hotspots were detected in Sumatra and 354 in Kalimantan.
Dry weather is expected to continue across most of southern Asean, except northern Peninsular Malaysia and Sumatra, where rain is forecast. Prolonged dry conditions could lead to an increase in hotspots and haze, raising the possibility of transboundary haze, NRES said.
At the Asean level, Alert Level 2 was activated on Aug 3. Countries in southern Asean — Brunei, Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Timor-Leste — are required to submit daily reports and emergency responses on fires, haze and measures taken.
NRES, together with the Department of Environment and Malaysian Meteorological Department, will continue monitoring and reporting developments in the weather, air quality and haze situation.
Relevant ministries, departments and agencies will also implement measures outlined under the National Haze Action Plan and National Open Burning Action Plan based on the alert level.
Members of the public in affected areas are advised to reduce outdoor activities, wear face masks and drink sufficient water to stay hydrated.
Open burning is also prohibited to prevent the haze situation from worsening.

Title: Immigration blames airline systems for long-validity passport headaches
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Aug 12 — Difficulties experienced by holders of Malaysian International Passports (PMA) with validity periods exceeding 10 years while travelling abroad were caused by systems used by certain airlines, rather than the immigration control systems of foreign countries, according to the Immigration Department.
Immigration director-general Datuk Zakaria Shaaban said that, in terms of border controls and International Civil Aviation Organisation (ICAO) standards, passports with validity periods exceeding 10 years did not pose a problem.
“It is not the country, it is the airlines. The immigration systems of any country do not have an issue with the validity period because they will simply enter the passport’s validity period.
“From the ICAO perspective and aviation standards, there is no issue... but the airlines have a problem,” he said when contacted by Bernama today.
Zakaria said the issue involved, among other things, systems used by airlines that set the maximum passport validity period at 10 years.
In this regard, Zakaria said Malaysia would bring the matter to ICAO for coordination with airlines, but no timeframe could be given for resolving the issue as it falls outside the department’s jurisdiction.
He explained that the department was still issuing PMAs with a 10-year validity and had only stopped granting additional validity carried forward from the previous passport that resulted in the overall validity of the new passport exceeding 10 years.
According to him, previously, applicants who renewed their passports early could receive an extension of up to six months based on the remaining validity of their old passports, resulting in the new passport having a validity period of up to 10 years and six months.
“After this, if they renew early, they will no longer get the extra period. They will get 10 years only. It will stop at 10 years,” he said.
Zakaria said existing passport holders whose passports have validity periods exceeding 10 years could obtain replacement passports free of charge.
He said the department would also issue a notice to all airlines to facilitate matters for Malaysians currently travelling abroad.
Regarding the number of 10-year PMAs issued since they were introduced on July 1, Zakaria said about 38,000 passports had been issued so far, of which 26,000 had validity periods exceeding 10 years. — Bernama
