Title: Court of Appeal says Malaysia is not the right forum for 1MDB suit against UK law firm White & Case
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Aug 12 — The Court of Appeal today granted an appeal by UK law firm White & Case LLP against a High Court ruling that allowed a lawsuit filed by 1Malaysia Development Berhad (1MDB) on alleged fraud to be heard in Malaysia.
In a unanimous decision, a three-judge panel chaired by Justice Datuk Alwi Abdul Wahab, sitting with Justices K. Muniandy and Datuk Aliza Sulaiman, ruled that the Kuala Lumpur High Court lacked the jurisdiction to hear 1MDB’s suit against the firm.
In delivering the court’s decision, Justice Muniandy said the panel found that the requirements under the Courts of Judicature Act 1964 and the Rules of Court 2012 for the service of proceedings outside Malaysia had not been satisfied.
“The respondent (1MDB) failed to prove that Malaysia is clearly the forum convenient to hear this suit,” he said.
Justice Muniandy added that Patrick Mahony, a director of PetroSaudi International Ltd, is a foreign national residing outside Malaysia and therefore could not serve as a proper “anchor defendant” to justify the service of proceedings out of jurisdiction.
The panel also set aside the High Court’s decision to consolidate 1MDB’s suit against White & Case with a separate suit filed by the sovereign wealth fund against several other defendants, including Deutsche Bank and PetroSaudi International.
“We agree with the appellant that the application for consolidation by the respondent was an unequivocal tactical manoeuvre,” Justice Muniandy said.
The court ordered 1MDB to pay RM130,000 in costs to White & Case.
Meanwhile, 1MDB’s counsel Datuk Lim Chee Wee informed the bench that he had received instructions from his client to seek leave to appeal today’s decision at the Federal Court.
1MDB filed a suit in the Kuala Lumpur High Court in 2024, seeking US$1.83 billion and US$33 million in losses from White & Case and Mahony.
The fund alleges that White & Case assisted PetroSaudi in committing fraud and conspired to harm 1MDB while acting as its legal counsel.
The alleged misconduct relates to two corporate transactions: the 2009 joint venture with PetroSaudi International, known as the Good Star phase, and the 2010 restructuring of 1MDB’s stake in the joint venture, which 1MDB claims resulted in significant financial losses.
The writ of summons was served out of jurisdiction on White & Case at their UK offices, and the firm subsequently applied to set aside the service, seeking a declaration that the Malaysian court had no jurisdiction to hear the suit.
Last year, the High Court rejected White & Case’s challenge, ruling that it could hear the lawsuit because the trial witnesses are located in Malaysia. The law firm then appealed this decision to the Court of Appeal.
White & Case is also appealing another High Court decision that ordered this lawsuit to be consolidated with a separate one filed by 1MDB against several other defendants, including Deutsche Bank and PetroSaudi International.
At the Court of Appeal today, lawyer Datuk Cyrus Das appeared for the firm. — Bernama

Title: RM200,000-plus aid for family of cop killed in Sabah electric shock incident, says home minister
Article:
KOTA BHARU, Aug 12 — The Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) will expedite benefits and welfare assistance for the family of Corporal Mohamad Nur Hafiz Rahim, 29, who died in an electric shock incident in Beaufort, Sabah, last Thursday.
Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said the move was aimed at easing the burden on the deceased’s wife, who is raising their two-year-old son.
He said today’s visit to the late officer’s family home, accompanied by Bukit Aman Management director Datuk Seri Abdul Aziz Abdul Majid, Kelantan police chief Datuk Mohd Yusoff Mamat and Sabah deputy police commissioner Datuk Mohd Azhar Hamin, was also a gesture of sympathy from the entire police force.
“We are here to convey the sympathies of the entire police force to the family of the deceased. The loss of any officer, regardless of rank or position, is a great loss to the police force,” he told reporters after visiting the family at their home in Kampung Hutan Pasir, Ketereh, here.
Saifuddin Nasution said the assistance presented included contributions from the Sabah and Kelantan Police Contingents (IPK), as well as takaful payments from the deceased’s contributions as a member of the Police Cooperative, with total contributions and payments exceeding RM200,000.
He said the deceased had named his wife, Fatimah Shahira, as the beneficiary of his monthly pension, while his mother was also named as a pension recipient.
He added that he had instructed the Bukit Aman Management director to expedite other payments due to the family and assured them that the process would not be subjected to the standard procedure.
“I personally assured the wife and family that all matters relating to the process will be expedited and will not go through the standard procedure,” he said.
Saifuddin Nasution also said the deceased’s wife could contact the IPK should she require further assistance concerning the welfare of her child and family.
Mohamad Nur Hafiz and two other officers, Corporal Chiu Teck Siong, 40, and Constable Muhammad Raimi Ismarubee, 26, died at about 5.50 pm last Thursday after they were believed to have suffered electric shocks while moving a metal pole outside the Weston Police Station near Sekolah Kebangsaan (SK) Weston, Beaufort, Sabah. — Bernama

Title: Malaysia, Saudi Arabia sign pact to share judicial know-how
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Aug 12 — Malaysia and Saudi Arabia today signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) to strengthen cooperation in the judicial field.
The MoU was signed by Chief Registrar of the Federal Court of Malaysia Azhaniz Teh Azman Teh and Saudi Arabian Minister of Justice Sheikh Dr Waleed Mohammed Alsmani at the Palace of Justice here.
The MoU signing, witnessed by Chief Justice Tun Wan Ahmad Farid Wan Salleh, was held in conjunction with Sheikh Dr Waleed’s official visit to Malaysia.
According to a statement issued by the Office of the Chief Registrar, the MoU provides a framework for closer cooperation in various areas, including civil case management, judicial technology and digitalisation, the exchange of practical experience and publicly available judicial information, institutional visits and regular exchanges.
It said the MoU marked an important milestone in Malaysia-Saudi Arabia judicial relations by providing a structured platform for closer institutional engagement, knowledge-sharing and continued cooperation towards the efficient administration of justice.
“The Malaysian Judiciary looks forward to the successful implementation of the areas of cooperation set out in the MoU and to further strengthening the longstanding ties between Malaysia and Saudi Arabia,” the statement said.
On the visit, the statement said it reflected the longstanding cordial relations between Malaysia and Saudi Arabia as well as their shared commitment to strengthening judicial cooperation and knowledge-sharing.
The programme also included a courtesy call on Tun Wan Ahmad Farid followed by a judicial dialogue and experience sharing session focusing on Malaysia’s judicial approach to sexual offences against children and the digitalisation of the Judiciary through the e-Court system. — Bernama

Title: Airport security plan heads to Cabinet next week after Malaysian pilot's drug bust
Article:
KOTA BHARU, Aug 12 — A plan to enhance airport security controls will be presented to the Cabinet next week following the arrest of a Malaysian pilot in Indonesia on suspicion of drug smuggling, said Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail.
He said the matter was discussed at last week’s Cabinet meeting, which instructed all relevant regulatory agencies to draw up plans to strengthen airport security.
The agencies included the Home Ministry, Transport Ministry, Border Control and Protection Agency (AKPS), Aviation Security, Malaysia Aviation Commission (MAVCOM) and the Civil Aviation Authority of Malaysia (CAAM), he said.
“The agencies met yesterday, and I understand that a paper on the plan to enhance airport security controls will be presented to the Cabinet at next week’s meeting,” he told reporters after visiting the family of the late Cpl Mohamad Nur Hafiz Rahim in Ketereh here today.
Mohamad Nur Hafiz was believed to have died from an electric shock in Beaufort, Sabah last week.
Saifuddin Nasution said the plan would cover coordination, training, infrastructure and logistics, including the control and operation of scanning machines.
He said airport scanning machines were operated by the AVSEC team in accordance with standards set by the International Civil Aviation Organisation (ICAO), with emphasis on detecting bombs, sharp weapons and firearms.
“If contraband appears on the screen, it can certainly be detected by the scanning machine. However, the screening procedures do not fall under the routine security checks carried out by the police or AKPS, so we need to realign the procedures,” he said.
He said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim had raised the matter with His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, who had urged all parties involved to give priority to airport security.
He added that the matter was not only about security but also the country’s reputation, particularly as Malaysia had recorded strong tourist arrival figures.
The 39-year-old Malaysian pilot was arrested by Indonesian authorities at Terminal 3 of Soekarno-Hatta International Airport on suspicion of attempting to smuggle 25 kilogrammes of drugs. — Bernama

Title: Worried govt producing GMO rice? Agriculture Ministry says Perak run is only a controlled test
Article:
SERDANG, Aug 12 — The proposed genetically modified rice field trial in Perak involving the MR219 variety is only a controlled test plot and does not constitute approval for the use of genetically modified organism (GMO) crops in Malaysia, said Agriculture and Food Security Ministry (KPKM) secretary-general Datuk Seri Isham Ishak.
He said the trial was intended to generate scientific evidence and data on GMO, particularly its potential role in addressing food security challenges, rather than to allow its commercial use.
“So we are not allowing GMO to be used, but we need to understand how GMO can perhaps in the future provide for food security.
“If we don’t do this (test), then we don’t know. So that is why there’s a test plot. It’s not an official plot,” he said during a press conference on the Malaysia Agriculture, Horticulture and Agrotourism Exhibition (Maha) 2026 here today.
He was responding to concerns raised by a group of organisations who had called on the government to reject the proposed field trial involving MR219 in Kampung Kepayang, Perak, citing concerns over food safety, environmental contamination and increased herbicide use.
Isham assured that the test plot would be conducted under controlled, monitored and documented conditions to ensure that any potential issues would not spread beyond the trial area.
“So test plot is something that is controlled, is monitored, recorded, so that it doesn’t… if there’s any issues with the plot, then it doesn’t spread over,” he said.
He said exploring ways to increase productivity was vital to Malaysia’s food security strategy, as the nation continues to grapple with the challenge of maintaining sufficient agricultural land while meeting the food needs of a growing population.
“So currently there’s a lot of pressure in terms of land use. So there is the pressure for land development for housing, for business, for industrial. And there’s also pressure for us to maintain our land acreage to ensure the sustainability and also food security for a long period of time.
“Agriculture use land is slowly being taken over by development, but we need to make sure we can still maintain feeding 34 million people.... with the current land acreage, can they (available land) fulfil that mandate?,” he questioned. — Bernama

Title: Property crime pushes Pahang crime index higher in first seven months of 2026
Article:
KUANTAN, Aug 12 — The Pahang crime index increased by 105 cases to 1,262 cases from January to July this year, compared to 1,157 cases for the same period last year.
Acting Pahang police chief Datuk Azry Akmar Ayob said the rate of resolving crime cases decreased to 59.58 per cent from 71.74 per cent.
“The increase (in crime index) was mainly driven by the rise in property crime cases, which increased to 1,023 cases, compared to 914 cases during the same period last year,” he said when speaking at the Pahang police contingent headquarters (IPK) monthly assembly here today.
He said the Pahang Narcotics Crime Investigation Department (JSJN) recorded 8,277 arrests in the first seven months of this year, compared to 8,243 arrests last year whereas the value of drug seizures decreased significantly to RM8.95 million, compared to RM25.8 million in the same period.
Meanwhile, he said the Pahang Commercial Crime Investigation Department (JSJK) opened 1,893 investigation papers from January to July this year, compared to 1,658 in the same period in 2025.
“A total of 1,380 arrests were made compared to 1,167 arrests last year, while the number of charge sheets increased to 769 from 633,” he said.
Azry Akmar said that although the number of commercial cases increased, the recorded loss value decreased 9.8 per cent to RM46.3 million, compared to RM51.3 million last year.
In an effort to assist scam victims, he said the Pahang JSJK via the National Scam Response Centre (NSRC) had seized RM355,355.15, with RM134,546.70 or 37.9 per cent of that amount being returned to the victims.
In terms of traffic aspects, he said the number of road accidents increased to 14,640 cases compared to 14,016 cases last year but the number of fatal accidents decreased to 242 cases compared to 265 cases in the same period.
He added that a total of 129,451 summonses for various traffic offences were issued by the Pahang Traffic Investigation and Enforcement Department (JSPT), with a total compound collection of RM4.94 million. — Bernama

Title: Fahmi: Govt raises RM48m in sponsorships for Merdeka, Malaysia Day celebrations
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Aug 12 — Sponsorships for this year’s Merdeka and Malaysia Day celebrations have risen to more than RM48 million, Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil announced today, describing the contributions as a “public-private partnership” success.
Of the total, RM2.7 million was contributed in cash, while the remaining RM45.93 million comprised contributions in the form of goods and services.
“The ministry is deeply honoured to announce that the total value of sponsorship for HKHM 2026, as verified by the Ministry of Communications Sponsorship Committee to date, amounts to RM48.63 million,” the minister said at an event to celebrate the sponsors here.
“This amount represents a highly encouraging increase of more than 118 per cent compared to last year, which was RM22.3 million.”
MORE TO COME

Title: Perak DAP says it will remain in unity govt, back Anwar’s reform agenda
Article:
IPOH, Aug 12 — Perak DAP has unanimously decided to remain in the Unity Government and mobilise the party’s entire machinery to fulfil the people’s mandate and continue the country’s reform agenda.
In a statement today, Perak DAP said the decision was made to deliver on its election promises under the leadership of Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.
According to the statement, Anwar’s leadership had proven successful in implementing various reforms over the past three years, while also enhancing the country’s image and standing on the world stage.
“DAP must continue to demonstrate its capabilities through achievements and work performance so as not to disappoint the people’s expectations.
“By remaining in the government, we can continue implementing the Pakatan Harapan manifesto, including institutional reforms, judicial independence, efforts to combat corruption, reducing the cost of living, reforming the national revenue system, and safeguarding the rights and freedoms of Malaysia’s multiracial society,” the statement said.
Perak DAP stressed the need to fully realise the policies during the current term in order to drive reforms and spur national development for the people’s well-being despite facing various challenges.
The party also remains committed to mobilising all its strength to fulfil the people’s mandate while staying true to the aspirations of the “Malaysia for Malaysians” struggle and remaining mindful of its responsibility to that cause.
The statement also stressed that, in order to safeguard the political strength of an inclusive and progressive multiracial society, DAP needs to remain in the Unity Government to provide a balance and prevent extremist forces from continuing to gain ground.
“Malaysia has witnessed four changes of prime minister over the past seven years. Political instability has affected the economy and investor confidence. That bitter experience must not be repeated, and therefore DAP must not disappoint the mandate given by the people.
“The party must shoulder the responsibility of remaining in the Unity Government until the end of the term to maintain political stability, implement reforms, demonstrate achievements and regain the people’s confidence. This is the right and responsible path,” the statement said.
The position was expressed ahead of the 2026 DAP Party Conference this Sunday, which will determine whether the party remains in or leaves the federal government for the remainder of the current parliamentary term. A motion on the matter will be tabled by DAP secretary-general Anthony Loke.
The motion will be decided through a vote involving 4,264 delegates from 1,704 eligible branches attending the conference at the Putrajaya International Convention Centre. — Bernama

Title: Ipoh married couple charged with trafficking 480.6g MDMA, face death penalty
Article:
IPOH, Aug 12 — A married couple was charged at the Magistrate’s Court here today with trafficking 480.6 grammes of Methylenedioxymethamphetamine (MDMA) last week.
Teoh Wai Loon, 44, and Lim Suk Pei, 38, nodded in understanding after the charge was read out before Magistrate S. Punitha, but no plea was recorded as the case falls under the High Court jurisdiction.
According to the charge, they were jointly accused of trafficking 480.6 grammes of MDMA at Room M333, The Pearl Orient Sdn Bhd, Bercham Bistari 4, Medan Bercham Bistari, in the Kinta district, at about 10.30 pm on Aug 4.
The charge was framed under Section 39B(1)(a) of the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952, read together with Section 34 of the Penal Code, and punishable under Section 39B(2) of the same Act, which provides for the death penalty or life imprisonment and whipping of not less than 12 strokes if the death penalty is not imposed, upon conviction.
The prosecution was conducted by Deputy Public Prosecutor Muhammad Zulqarnain Wan Asmira, while both accused were unrepresented.
The court set Dec 7 for case mention to obtain the chemical analysis report.
On Aug 6, police arrested seven individuals, including the couple, for allegedly being involved in a drug trafficking syndicate that had been active since June, following four raids in Ipoh and Tapah.
During the raids, police seized ketamine and MDMA, including about 2.6 kilogrammes of MDMA found at two houses in Tapah.
The drugs seized were estimated to be worth RM538,451, in addition to three vehicles worth RM224,000 and RM32,376 in cash. — Bernama

Title: Malaysia brings foreign ambassadors to Sabah’s east coast to boost security confidence, tourism
Article:
KOTA BHARU, Aug 12 — The government is taking a direct approach to rebuilding international confidence in Sabah’s east coast by bringing foreign ambassadors and representatives to assess the security situation firsthand, almost 13 years after the Lahad Datu incident.
Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said the effort was important as the incident in Sabah had left an impact not only on the local community but also on the area’s tourism potential.
He said the Eastern Sabah Security Command (ESSCOM), which covers 10 districts along Sabah’s east coast and brings together three main agencies, was responsible for ensuring that the security situation in the area returned to normal.
Saifuddin Nasution said the area had vast tourism potential, with its islands, beaches, rivers and forests contributing to local economic activities.
“We have been working on this for almost 13 years and, with the situation now much better and more reassuring, we need to conduct an outreach programme to restore foreign countries’ confidence in the security situation,” he said after visiting the family of Corporal Mohamad Nur Hafiz Rahim, who died in a suspected electrocution incident in Beaufort, Sabah, at their home in Kampung Hutan Pasir, Ketereh, here today.
Saifuddin Nasution said under the programme, foreign ambassadors and delegates were taken on a three-day, two-night visit to Sabah’s east coast, including visits to the forests and islands, to see for themselves the security situation and gain firsthand experience of the area.
He hoped the approach would lead the countries involved to review their respective travel advisories for their citizens.
“This is the third year since we started the programme, and several countries have indeed changed or revised their travel advisories for their citizens,” he said.
Saifuddin Nasution said the United States and Japan were among the countries that had revised their travel advisories, while China topped the list of tourist arrivals to Sabah’s east coast, followed by European countries, particularly Germany and the United Kingdom, as well as East Asian countries.
He said there had been a significant increase in tourist arrivals to Sabah’s east coast after three years of implementing the programme and following reviews of travel advisories by the countries involved.
Saifuddin Nasution said the increase in tourist arrivals was also seen among those travelling via the Kuala Lumpur-Kota Kinabalu and Kota Kinabalu-Tawau routes, as well as direct flights to Tawau. — Bernama

Title: Sarawak caregiver in the dock over fractured arm of baby just 20 days old
Article:
KUCHING, Aug 12 — A 29-year-old woman claimed trial at the Sessions Court here today to a charge of causing injury to a 20-day-old baby at a confinement centre here last week.
The accused, from Puncak Borneo, pleaded not guilty before Judge Noorhisham Mohd Jaafar after she was charged under Section 31(1)(a) of the Child Act 2001 (Act 611).
The offence carries a fine of up to RM50,000, imprisonment for up to 20 years, or both, upon conviction.
The court then granted the accused a court bail of RM10,000 with two local sureties and her to report to a police station once a month.
The case was fixed for pre-trial case management on Sept 14.
The charge alleged that the accused, who was entrusted with the care of the baby, had negligently handled and lifted the child from a baby cot in a manner likely to cause physical injury.
The incident was alleged to have occurred between 12.30am and 1.30am at a confinement centre here on Aug 4.
The baby was alleged to have sustained a closed fracture of the right humerus.
Deputy public prosecutor Adriana Maisarah Mohd Farid appeared for the prosecution, while the accused was represented by counsel Roger Chin. — The Borneo Post

Title: Maritime expert: Port businesses hit hard by uncertainty over commingled oil tax
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 12 — Businesses involved in the shipping and petroleum sectors are being badly affected by uncertainty over the tax treatment of oil cargo commingled in shore tanks at Johor’s Tanjung Langsat Port, said Maritime Network Sdn Bhd chief executive officer Datuk Seri Jeyenderan Ramasamy.
He said the Royal Malaysian Customs Department (JKDM) must urgently provide a clear ruling on whether such commingling is permissible and, if so, how the cargo should be classified, documented and assessed for tax purposes.
With more than 30 years of maritime experience, Jeyenderan said the issue was particularly important at Tanjung Langsat Port, where petroleum cargo is handled and may be discharged from vessels into shore tanks during transshipment operations.
“While commingling could be part of operational practices, the absence of clear guidelines on its regulatory and tax implications could expose businesses to uncertainty, additional costs and potential disputes with the authorities. When different consignments are mixed in a shore tank, Customs must be able to determine whether the commingling is correct and how the cargo should subsequently be treated for tax purposes.
“Customs needed to establish clear requirements covering documentation, cargo classification, valuation and tax assessment to ensure businesses knew exactly what was expected of them. Companies should not be left to interpret tax and customs requirements on their own, particularly when the outcome could have significant financial implications for their operations.
“If the practice is allowed, customs should clearly state the requirements. If there is tax to be paid, businesses must know exactly how it is calculated. If it is not taxable under the applicable rules, that should also be clearly stated,” he said in a statement today.
Jeyenderan stressed that prolonged uncertainty could result in cargo delays, additional storage and operational costs, contractual complications and disruption to business activities at the port.
He said legitimate companies should not be placed at a disadvantage or face unexpected financial exposure because of unclear regulatory or tax requirements.
“We are not asking for special treatment. We are asking for clarity. Businesses need to know what is permitted, what documentation is required and what tax treatment applies,” he said.
Jeyenderan also urged customs to engage directly with industry players to better understand actual operations involving petroleum cargo at Tanjung Langsat Port, particularly processes that take place after vessel discharge and during storage and transshipment.
Jeyenderan had earlier raised concerns over what he alleged was the practice of oil cargo being commingled in shore tanks following vessel discharge during transshipment operations, saying it could give rise to regulatory, documentation and tax compliance issues if not properly managed.
He said when crude oil from different consignments was mixed in shore tanks, the physical characteristics of the cargo could change and, unless the accompanying documentation was properly updated, discrepancies could arise in cargo classification, valuation and tax assessment.

Title: National Day flypast means brief KLIA flight pauses – here’s when
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Aug 12 — The Civil Aviation Authority of Malaysia (CAAM) today announced the closure of airspace within the Kuala Lumpur Terminal Control Area from Aug 26 to 29, and Aug 31 to facilitate rehearsals and the National Day flypast in Putrajaya.
In a statement, CAAM said during the closure periods, scheduled aeroplane take-offs and landings at Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) will be temporarily suspended to ensure the safe and orderly conduct of the rehearsals and flypast.
The airspace closure schedule for rehearsals and the National Day Flypast 2026 is as follows:
From Aug 26 to 28, the airspace will be closed from 11am to noon for rehearsals.
On Aug 29, a full rehearsal will be conducted from 8.45 am to 9.45 am.
On Aug 31, the National Day Flypast will take place from 8.45 am to 9.45 am.
Passengers travelling through KLIA during these periods are advised to check the latest status and schedule of their flights directly with the respective airlines, as some flights may be rescheduled or otherwise affected by the temporary suspension of aeroplane movements.
“CAAM would also like to remind the public that all drone or Unmanned Aircraft System operations are strictly prohibited within the affected areas during the rehearsals and National Day Flypast.
“Unauthorised drone operations pose a serious safety risk, particularly to aircraft operating at lower altitudes and may result in enforcement action under the Civil Aviation Regulations 2016,” it added.
CAAM appreciates the understanding and continued cooperation of passengers airlines, airspace users and members of the public during this period.
These temporary measures are necessary to ensure the safe and orderly conduct of the National Day Flypast while safeguarding the safety, security and efficiency of Malaysia’s airspace. — Bernama

Title: Selangor wants one body to get Greater Klang Valley projects moving together
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Aug 12 — The Selangor state government is streamlining its metropolitan governance model through the proposed establishment of the Selangor Metropolitan Corporation (PMS) to coordinate development planning across multiple local authority (PBT) jurisdictions.
State Local Government and Tourism Committee chairman Datuk Ng Suee Lim said the proposal was part of the Selangor Greater Klang Valley (SGKV) initiative, with the PMS serving as the coordinating body for the planning, development and implementation of projects involving more than one PBT.
“To support the implementation of the model, the state government proposes the establishment of PMS as a state-level coordinating mechanism.
“The establishment of PMS will not change the jurisdiction or functions of PBTs under the Local Government Act 1976. Instead, it will strengthen coordination between the state government, PBTs and relevant agencies in addressing development issues spanning (PBT) administrative boundaries,” he said.
He said this in response to a question from Danial Al-Rashid Haron Aminar Rashid (PH-Batu Tiga) on the progress of the SGKV development at the Selangor State Legislative Assembly today.
Meanwhile, Ng said the proposal to establish PMS had been submitted to the Housing and Local Government Ministry, with further discussions being held with relevant federal government agencies, particularly on legal, governance and implementation aspects.
“Once the process is completed, the PMS Establishment Enactment Bill will be finalised before being tabled in the Selangor State Assembly in accordance with the legal procedures in force,” he said.
At the same time, Ng said the SGKV 2035 Blueprint, which was now nearing finalisation, would serve as a strategic document setting the direction for development and guiding the implementation of the Selangor metropolitan governance model. — Bernama

Title: Hainan, here we come: Penang gets new direct China flight in Oct
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Aug 12 — The Haikou-Penang direct flight service will be launched on Oct 11, making Haikou the ninth Chinese city to have a scheduled direct air link with Penang, said State Tourism and Creative Economy Committee chairman Wong Hon Wai.
He said the new route would further strengthen air connectivity between Hainan and Penang while opening up greater opportunities for Penang to tap into the China tourism market.
Wong said this following a meeting with representatives of Hainan Airlines in Guangzhou today, held on the sidelines of his tourism roadshow to showcase Penang’s tourism offerings.
He said in a statement today that both parties had discussed and finalised plans for the new route.
“Haikou will become the ninth Chinese city with a scheduled direct air connection to Penang, further strengthening Penang’s air connectivity with China.
“Following Guangzhou, Xiamen, Chengdu, Shenzhen, Shanghai, Qingdao and Chongqing, the addition of Haikou marks another important milestone in the continued expansion of Penang’s air links with major cities in China,” said Wong.
The inaugural direct flight, HU477, is scheduled to depart from Haikou Meilan International Airport (HAK) at 5.30 pm on Oct 11 and arrive at Penang International Airport (PEN) at 8.45 pm the same day.
The return flight, HU478, will depart from Penang International Airport at 9.45 pm on the same day and arrive at Haikou Meilan International Airport at 1 am the following day.
The service will operate twice weekly on Wednesdays and Sundays.
He said the new route would further enhance Penang’s accessibility as an international tourism destination, consolidate its existing China tourist market and create more favourable conditions for the state to tap into the vast potential of China, one of the world’s largest tourism markets.
Wong said Haikou represented a market with significant potential for Penang, noting that China’s National Bureau of Statistics recorded Haikou’s permanent resident population at 3.0563 million as at the end of 2025, while Hainan Province had approximately 10.55 million permanent residents.
“As the capital of Hainan Province, Haikou serves as an important gateway connecting Hainan with the outside world. For Penang, this represents a tourism market with considerable potential for further development,” he said.
Wong said the new air link would have significance beyond tourism, particularly in strengthening the longstanding friendly ties between Penang and Hainan.
The two cities established friendly state-to-province relations in 2013, followed by the strengthening of ties between Penang Island and Sanya City through the signing of a memorandum of understanding on friendly city relations in 2017.
He said improved accessibility and greater ease of travel would help deepen cooperation between Penang and Hainan in areas including business, creative industries, culture, people-to-people exchanges and tourism.
Wong also highlighted the broader potential for economic and industrial exchanges, noting that the Hainan Free Trade Port was an important free trade platform in China, while Penang was an important electronics manufacturing and semiconductor hub in Malaysia, as well as a regional logistics node.
“With the establishment of a scheduled direct flight between Haikou and Penang, businesses and industry players on both sides will have more convenient access for business travel, industrial exchanges and logistics connectivity,” he added. — Bernama

Title: PMX expected home today after hernia procedure, says wife
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 12 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim is expected to be discharged from hospital today after receiving treatment, his wife Datuk Seri Dr Wan Azizah Wan Ismail said.
She said Anwar expressed his appreciation to everyone who had prayed for his health and well-being.
“PMX sends his regards and thanked everyone who has prayed for his health and recovery,” she said.
She spoke to reporters after attending the Semarak Merdeka programme in conjunction with the 2026 National Month celebrations at the Bandar Tun Razak branch of the Kuala Lumpur City Hall (DBKL) here.
Anwar had successfully undergone an elective laparoscopic surgical procedure to treat a para-umbilical hernia on Monday. — Bernama

Title: Minister Zulkifli Hasan: Tabung Haji to face tougher oversight as govt acts on RCI findings
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 12 — The government’s pledge to leave no stone unturned in strengthening Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) through stricter policy and regulatory measures to ensure that similar issues do not recur was among the messages at yesterday’s special Dewan Rakyat sitting.
The government explained how amendments to the Tabung Haji Act 1955 will be implemented in line with the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) at the special sitting which lasted more than 10 hours.
Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Religious Affairs) Dr Zulkifli Hasan said a task force was established to examine the RCI’s findings and recommendations when tabling the report.
It will be headed by TH chairman Tan Sri Abdul Rashid Hussain and comprises Bank Negara Governor Datuk Seri Abdul Rasheed Ghaffour and Securities Commission (SC) chairman Datuk Mohammad Faiz Azmi.
“I was informed that the task force has agreed to recommend that the management of TH’s funds and investments be regulated by the SC, while matters relating to the management of the haj pilgrimage will be regulated by the Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Religious Affairs), with TH remaining as an intact entity.
“Further details of the recommendation will be provided to me for further consideration before being presented to the Cabinet for approval,” he said at the special sitting.
He also presented details concerning 14 troubled investments, efforts to prosecute those involved, and what TH’s financial situation would have been like had it not been rescued through a bailout, as well as panic withdrawals by depositors due to a loss of confidence at the time.
Zulkifli said TH’s losses had come close to RM13 billion, while the government faced the risk of assuming liabilities amounting to approximately RM74.5 billion in 2018 if large-scale panic withdrawals had occurred.
During the winding-up session, Finance Minister II Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah Azizan also detailed how seven of the 14 troubled investments had suffered 100 per cent losses, while TH’s investment in Putrajaya Perdana Bhd had indirectly drawn the institution into 1Malaysia Development Bhd (1MDB).
He stressed that the Madani Government was not concealing anything, even when the figures were painful.
He also said accountability would be upheld without favouritism, with investigations to be carried out comprehensively. There will be no compromise shown towards any party found guilty.
“Tabung Haji is being strengthened so that history does not repeat itself. Act 535 will be amended to legally prohibit active politicians from serving on the board of directors; its investments will be regulated by the SC; hibah (profit distributions) will be based on audited accounts; and every decision concerning TH will be measured against one benchmark only – the interests of the ummah,” said Amir Hamzah.
Earlier, a total of 39 Members of Parliament were given five minutes each to debate the issue.
Among the proposals put forward was the establishment of a single regulator for large non-bank financial institutions (NBFIs), placing them under the same supervisory framework.
The proposal by Aminolhuda Hassan (PH-Sri Gading) covered major NBFIs such as the Employees Provident Fund (EPF/KWSP), Permodalan Nasional Bhd (PNB), Retirement Fund Incorporated (KWAP), the Armed Forces Fund Board (LTAT), and TH.
According to him, Malaysia currently does not have a single authority responsible for prudential supervision, systemic risk assessment and governance oversight of the non-bank financial sector.
Meanwhile, Bentong MP Young Syefura Othman (PH) called on the government to detail measures to reduce TH’s dependence on income from UJSB sukuk, which, according to the RCI Report, contributed nearly 26 per cent of the institution’s annual income.
The 211-page RCI report was made public on July 29. It contained various findings concerning weaknesses in the management and operations of the institution from 2014 to 2020.
The report also put forward 25 recommendations for improvements, 75 per cent of which had been implemented by TH as of July 30.
The government announced the establishment of the RCI in 2021, followed by the appointment of its members on Jan 20, 2022. The RCI report was subsequently presented to the Yang di-Pertuan Agong on Aug 30, 2022. — Bernama

Title: When losing money is winning: Selangor's plastic bag charges plummet
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Aug 12 —The collection of plastic bag charges received by the Selangor Government has shown a consistent downward trend over a three-year period, from RM13.35 million in 2023 to RM6.97 million in 2025.
State Public Health and Environment Exco Jamaliah Jamaluddin said the total collection in 2024 was recorded at RM9.04 million, bringing the total collection for the period 2023 to 2025 to RM29.36 million.
She said the drop in collection by almost half reflected changes in consumer behavior, which increasingly prioritised the use of reusable bags when shopping, in line with efforts to reduce the use of single-use plastic bags.
“Based on these developments, the state government believes that the Plastic-Free Campaign and the Plastic Bag Charge Collection Programme have succeeded in raising public awareness and encouraging the use of reusable bags.
“The trend of decreasing plastic bag charge collection also shows a change in consumer behavior towards reducing the use of single-use plastic bags,” she said at the Selangor State Legislative Assembly Session today.
She was responding to a question by Leong Tuck Chee (PH-Pandamaran) on the effectiveness of the campaign to reduce the use of plastic bags and the amount of collection collected by the state government through the Plastic Bag Charge Collection Programme.
Jamaliah said the Plastic-Free Campaign began to be implemented since 2010 in Selangor and the Plastic Bag Charge Collection Programme in 2020 by the state government has shown positive developments in terms of consumer awareness, participation from the private sector, especially commercial premises and event organisers.
“Although there is no specific study that measures the reduction in the use of plastic bags as a whole, the state government is using the collection trend to encourage the Plastic Bag Charge Programme as one of the indicators of changing consumer behaviour,” she said. — Bernama

Title: More than nine-tenths of Kelantan land remains Malay reserve, top in peninsula, says MB
Article:
KOTA BHARU, Aug 12 — The total area of Malay reserve land in Kelantan is recorded at 526,083 hectares (ha) or 91.5 per cent, involving 816,020 ownerships as of June this year.
According to Kelantan Menteri Besar Datuk Mohd Nassuruddin Daud, the area of non-Malay reserve land is 48,344 ha or 8.4 per cent, involving 43,255 titles.
“Based on land administration records up to June 2026, the total area of land ownership in Kelantan is 574,427 ha, involving 859,275 titles.
“Alhamdulillah, Kelantan remains the state with the largest area of Malay reserve land compared to other states in Peninsular Malaysia,” he said.
He said this when answering a question from Datuk Abdul Rahman Yunus (PAS-Pasir Tumboh) regarding the current area of Malay reserve land in Kelantan during the State Legislative Assembly sitting at the Kota Darulnaim Complex here today.
Mohd Nassuruddin said that the figure is the adjusted total for all 11 districts, with more than nine-tenths of the total land ownership in the state falling under the Malay reserve category.
“In terms of area, Gua Musang recorded the largest Malay reserve land, which is 122,735 ha, followed by Pasir Mas (56,656 ha), Tanah Merah (56,246 ha) and Kuala Krai (53,473 ha).
“In terms of percentage, Tanah Merah recorded the highest rate at 99.9 per cent, followed by Tumpat, Pasir Puteh, Bachok, Pasir Mas, Kota Bharu and Jeli,” he said.
He said that there has been no reduction in the Malay reserve land in Kelantan, whereas Section 13A of the Kelantan Malay Reservations Enactment allows land ownership by non-Malays within the Malay reserve area.
He added that the same provision also grants state authorities the power to regulate transactions within Malay reserve areas, including prohibiting them if they jeopardise the interests of Malay reserves. — Bernama

Title: Six schools in Sarawak shift to online learning as haze hits ‘very unhealthy’ levels
Article:
KUCHING, Aug 12 — Six schools in the Tebedu district have been ordered to temporarily close after the Air Pollutant Index (API) reading there exceeded 200 amid worsening haze conditions.
The Sarawak Education Department (JPNS) said the precautionary measure was taken in line with the Education Ministry’s (MOE) guidelines, with the safety, health and wellbeing of students and school staff given priority.
As of 10.30am today, the schools involved are SK Sejijag, with 51 students and 14 staff; SK Sungai Sameran (129 students, 21 staff); SK Tepoi (42 students, 15 staff); SK Entubuh (67 students, 18 staff); SK Temong (205 students, 21 staff); and SK Tema (85 students, 15 staff).
According to JPNS, these schools are under the administration of the Serian District Education Office (Serian PPD).
JPNS also reminded principals and headmasters that they do not need to wait for specific instructions from the PPD or JPNS to close schools when the API reading in their respective areas or districts exceeds 200.
“Under MOE Circular No. 1 of 2019 on measures to safeguard the health and safety of students in schools located in areas considered critical due to haze, all schools in areas or districts where the API exceeds 200 must be closed immediately.
“Principals and headmasters must act promptly based on the current API readings in their respective areas and do not need to wait for closure instructions from the PPD or JPNS.
“At the same time, schools must inform the PPD and JPNS of the closure immediately for coordination, monitoring and record-keeping,” the department said.
JPNS said home-based teaching and learning (PdPR) would continue online during the temporary closure to ensure students’ learning was not disrupted.
The department added that schools have also been instructed to maintain communication with parents and guardians while giving due attention to the health and welfare of students throughout the closure.
Regarding the situation in Serian, whereby haze has also worsened, JPNS said the department through PPD Serian will continue monitoring API readings and air quality by obtaining updates from the authorities and relevant agencies.
Schools have also been reminded to closely monitor API readings in their respective areas and take appropriate action in accordance with MOE guidelines.
The department said the decision on the reopening of schools will take into account the latest API readings, prevailing conditions and directives or guidelines in force.
JPNS stressed that the safety and wellbeing of students and all education personnel remained its priority, adding that prompt and appropriate action based on established guidelines was necessary to minimise exposure to health risks caused by haze.
“Parents and guardians are urged to ensure their children remain safe and follow official updates issued by the schools, PPD Serian and JPNS.
“They are also advised not to rely on unofficial information or wait for additional instructions once a school had announced its closure based on an API reading exceeding 200,” added JPNS. — The Borneo Post

Title: Wong Chen joins Bersama after resigning as Subang MP
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 12 — Former Subang MP Wong Chen has joined Bersama, days after resigning from his parliamentary seat.
Bersama chairman Datuk Seri Rafizi Ramli announced Wong’s membership at a press conference at the party’s headquarters in Taman Putra Perdana, Puchong, today.
Wong, a three-term MP who had been with PKR for nearly two decades, had previously indicated that he would eventually leave the party after Rafizi and Nik Nazmi Nik Ahmad resigned their parliamentary seats to lead Bersama.
Wong was among three PKR MPs whose access to the MyKhas constituency funding portal was revoked after they attended Bersama’s launch event in May. The other two were Ampang MP Rodziah Ismail and Petaling Jaya MP Lee Chean Chung.
Wong was previously the non-executive chairman of Malaysia Debt Ventures Bhd but was removed from the position in May.

Title: MEF urges govt to act faster before MSME cash crunch turns into job losses
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 12 — The Malaysian Employers Federation (MEF) is calling on the government to strengthen assistance for micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs).
It noted that businesses continue to face pressures from rising operating and labour costs, financing constraints, weaker cash flows, supply-chain disruptions, regulatory requirements and intense market competition.
MEF president Datuk Dr Syed Hussain Syed Husman has proposed that the government consider introducing a coordinated MSME survival and resilience package to help businesses navigate ongoing cost and cash-flow pressures.
He said the package should include targeted and temporary tax relief, faster and simpler access to financing and greater use of cash-flow-based lending.
“Under this package, the government should consider expanding government-backed guarantees, temporary regulatory and compliance relief, faster payments to MSME suppliers, greater MSME access to government procurement and employment retention support,” he said in a statement today.
He stressed that MSME policy must ultimately be viewed through the lens of employment and economic sustainability.
“Helping viable MSMEs survive is itself an important way of protecting workers because these businesses provide employment to millions of Malaysians and support extensive domestic supply chains.
“Our objective is not to keep inefficient businesses alive indefinitely or prevent viable businesses from being pushed into closure because of temporary cash-flow and cost pressures beyond their control,” he said.
MEF said it is ready to work closely with the Ministry of Entrepreneur and Cooperative Development (KUSKOP), the Ministry of Finance (MoF), Bank Negara Malaysia (BNM) and other relevant agencies to ensure that MSME assistance is practical, accessible and responsive to actual business conditions.
“MSMEs have shown remarkable resilience through repeated economic challenges. They have continued to employ Malaysians, support local suppliers and contribute to the economy even when their own margins are under pressure.
“They now need a stronger and more comprehensive safety net. The government has already taken important steps. MEF’s call is for us to go further – faster, more targeted and with greater urgency – before temporary business difficulties become permanent closures and job losses,” added Syed Hussain. — Bernama

Title: Waiting for your university offer? UPUOnline results out Aug 14 noon
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Aug 12 — The results of applications for further studies at public universities (UA) via UPUOnline® for the Bachelor’s Degree level for the 2026/2027 Academic Session for STPM/equivalent holders will be announced on August 14.
Results can be checked from 12 noon, August 14 to 5 pm, August 23 online via the links https://upu.mohe.gov.my,
https://upu2.mohe.gov.my
and via the Mobile UPUPocket or Mobile MyGov applications on smartphones.
The Ministry of Higher Education (KPT) in a statement today announced that confirmation of acceptance or rejection of offers will begin from August 15 to 23 on the respective UA websites.
“Official offer letters will be issued by UA to successful candidates starting August 15 after the candidate confirms that they agree to accept the offer within the specified period.

https://upu.mohe.gov.my

Title: Selangor Rail Line still in planning stage, completion targeted for 2060
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Aug 12 — The Selangor government is still in the discussion stage with various parties including the private sector to identify the appropriate development and financing model for the development of the Selangor Rail Line.
State Investment, Trade and Mobility Exco Ng Sze Han said the state government through the Menteri Besar of Selangor (Incorporated) or MBI as the Technical Committee for Selangor Rail Development is examining the most potential development and financing model to be implemented.
He said the mechanism for implementing the development of the Selangor Rail Line is also being refined to identify the most profitable and appropriate method.
“Of course, a large-scale project like the Selangor Rail Line involves the private sector as well as government agencies,” he said in response to a question from Mariam Abdul Rashid (PH-Meru) regarding the direction of the Selangor Rail Line project at the Selangor State Legislative Assembly sitting today.
Meanwhile, he said based on the feasibility study that has been carried out, the first phase of the project’s development is expected to take 10 years, covering the entire development process including the preparation of preliminary designs, detailed studies and approval of the Railway Scheme by the Land Public Transport Agency (APAD).
“The phase also includes procurement, land acquisition, construction work and the testing and commissioning process.”
“The final phase of development is expected to be completed in 2060, subject to the implementation of the planned development phases,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Federal Court dismisses Kedah govt’s bid for leave to appeal in pool betting outlet licences case
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Aug 12 (Bernama) -- The Federal Court today dismissed the Kedah state government’s application seeking leave to appeal against a ruling that had quashed its decision to cease the issuance and renewal of business licences for pool betting operators in the state.
The three-judge panel chaired by Justice Datuk Rhodzariah Bujang, Datuk Collin Lawrence Sequerah and Datuk Azmi Ariffin ordered the state government to pay RM50,000 costs.
Justice Rhodzariah, who delivered the court’s unanimous decision, held that the state government has failed to meet the threshold requirement under Section 96 (a) of the Courts of Judicature Act 1964 for leave to be granted.
The Kedah Government had sought leave to appeal the Court of Appeal 2-1 majority decision, which upheld the High Court’s ruling in favour of pool betting agents, companies and their principal officers in challenging the state government’s directive.
The Court of Appeal, in its majority decision on Dec 12, 2025, ruled that the Kedah government’s decision to cease the issuance and renewal of business licences for pool betting operators was irrational and unconstitutional.
In the majority decision, Court of Appeal judge Datuk Faizah Jamaluddin said the decision by the state government to stop issuing and renewing pool betting business licences had exceeded the constitutional limits of the state power.
She said the decision was an impermissible state-wide prohibition of a subject matter reserved to the Federation.
However, in the dissenting judgment, Chief Judge of Sabah and Sarawak Datuk Azizah Nawawi held that the Kedah State Executive Council’s decision not to renew pool betting premises licences constituted a policy matter that should not be interfered with by the court.
She said the decision involved the state government’s discretion and consideration of the welfare of the people of Kedah above the personal interests of the operators.
Six judicial review applications were filed by pool betting agents, pool betting companies or principal officers of pool betting companies to challenge the state government’s decision.
On June 20, 2024, the High Court granted a declaration that the Kedah state government’s decision is ultra vires the Federal Constitution, a certiorari order to quash the decision and an order for damages to be assessed before the deputy registrar.
During Federal Court proceedings, counsel for the state government, Tan Sri Azhar Azizan Harun, sought leave to be granted and proposed six questions of law. He said the questions had not been determined by the top court and that it would be to public advantage if the court decide on those questions.
However, lawyer Brian Foong Mun Loong representing the pool betting operators, argued that the state government failed to fulfil the threshold requirement for leave to be granted.
In November 2021, Kedah Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Muhammad Sanusi Nor announced that the state would cease renewing local council licences for lottery outlets starting Jan 1, 2023, as part of efforts to curb social ills.
Speaking to reporters after the proceedings, Foong said the Federal Court’s decision to affirm the High Court’s ruling which quash the state government’s decision meant that his clients could now apply for business premises licences.
“As the policy has been quashed, technically, there is no reason for the local councils to refuse, he said.— Bernama

Title: High Court orders Rosmah to pay RM67.4m into stakeholder account pending appeal in missing jewellery suit
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 12 — Datin Seri Rosmah Mansor was today ordered by the High Court to pay RM67.4 million into a joint stakeholder account within a month, pending her appeal in a suit filed by Lebanese jeweller Global Royalty Trading SAL to recover the value of 43 jewellery items delivered to her.
Rosmah had previously sought to stay the execution of the High Court’s June 10 decision, with the court having fixed today to deliver its
decision
on the application.
In granting the order, Judicial Commissioner Marianne Antoinette Ghani said a stay was not automatically granted simply because an appeal was pending, further stating that Rosmah — as the defendant — had to prove special circumstances justified her application for a stay.
She said Rosmah’s contention that the judgment sum was too large for an individual to pay could not, by itself, justify a stay of execution, despite her claim that her jewellery had been seized during a raid by a third party.
“In the circumstances, the Court orders that a conditional stay of execution be granted to the defendant pending her appeal to the Court of Appeal.
“The defendant shall pay the judgment sum into a joint stakeholders account between the solicitors for the parties within one month from this order, failing which the plaintiff will be at liberty to take out execution proceedings as it deems fit in the circumstances pending the determination of the defendant’s appeal to the Court of Appeal,” she said.
In her judgment, Marianne said the court found that a conditional stay requiring the defendant to pay the judgment sum into a joint stakeholder account would best balance both parties’ rights.
“This will ensure that the plaintiff as the successful litigant is assured the fruit of its successful litigation and avoid the prejudice caused by an unconditional stay if the appeal is dismissed.
“Whilst ensuring that the defendant’s rights of appeal shall not be rendered nugatory should her appeal be allowed, as the judgement funds shall remain within the jurisdiction and are easily, therefore, recoverable, preventing her appeal from being rendered nugatory,” she said.
She also said the court was bound by a previous ruling which established that a substantial judgment sum, on its own, did not constitute a special circumstance.
Rosmah had previously argued that Global Royalty was a foreign entity with no business presence or assets in Malaysia, creating a real risk that the judgment sum could be transferred out of the jurisdiction or dissipated if she succeeded on appeal.
Lawyer Reza Rahim appeared for Rosmah while Datuk David Gurupatham appeared for Global Royalty.
The present case centred on 44 pieces of luxury jewellery worth RM67,461,027.37 (US$14.57 million) that Global Royalty said were delivered to Rosmah in 2018 for viewing under a consignment arrangement.
Global Royalty later filed a legal suit in 2023, seeking the return of the items or payment for their value after claiming the items were supplied to Rosmah on consignment but were never returned following their seizure during a 2018 police raid at Pavilion Residences.
Only one item — a diamond and emerald bracelet — was eventually recovered and returned to the Lebanese company following separate forfeiture proceedings.
